source_defaults.notes: Original Chatham News + Record weekly edition, explicitly dated February27-March4,2020 on the cover and questionnaire pages. The issue begins before the March3 primary; the URL upload timestamp is not used as publication evidence. The two Democratic questionnaire blocks on printed pagesB6-B7 (PDF pages20-21) were visually reviewed to separate candidate answers from reporter analysis and adjacent Republican columns. Candidate allegations, statistics and legislative-record claims are not independently adopted.

sources.speaker: David E. Price
sources.identity_notes: The visually checked pageB7 Democratic NC4 questionnaire names David Price and identifies him as the incumbent House member seeking reelection. This matches the canonical David E. Price record.

statements.quote: pass a comprehensive Medicare for All bill
statements.claim: Pledges a comprehensive Medicare for All bill and presents universal coverage as a central priority.
Calls for Medicaid expansion and protecting/improving the ACA on a path to universal coverage. This answer does not specify a public option or prove blanket opposition to single payer.
Calls for data protections and regulation, using European GDPR as a starting point. His description of existing privacy rules is not independent legal guidance.
Calls for comprehensive privacy/security legislation and clearer explanations of how companies store and use personal data.
Describes representation through presence, organizing and direct action alongside legislative work.
Emphasizes committee leadership and bipartisan passage of housing and transportation appropriations. This does not establish opposition to constituent organizing.

statements.quote: stop arms sales to Saudi Arabia
statements.claim: Calls for disengagement from Middle East wars, ending certain military support and redirecting resources toward rebuilding communities rather than controlling oil.

statements.quote: protect people displaced by conflict and climate change
statements.claim: Emphasizes diplomacy, democracy, the rule of law and protection for people displaced by conflict and climate change. No unmentioned weapons-transfer position is inferred.
Proposes a $15 minimum wage. No corresponding Price position is invented from silence in the selected answer.

statements.quote: at least one free hot meal to students per day
statements.claim: Proposes free school meals, facility improvements and more social workers/counselors, alongside changes to school-resource-officer deployment. This is not confused with the separate question of college affordability.
Supports campaign-finance disclosure, Super PAC donor transparency and public financing to reduce special-interest influence.

comparisons.analysis: Lockwood specifies Medicare for All; Price emphasizes ACA protection and Medicaid expansion toward universal coverage. Lockwood's separate campaign criticism of Price is not used as proof that Price opposes every single-payer proposal.

Both advocate stronger federal privacy protections. Lockwood names GDPR as a reference while Price emphasizes comprehensive legislation and clearer data-use disclosures; the shared goal does not make their full legal designs identical.

Lockwood foregrounds direct action and community organizing; Price foregrounds institutional leadership and bipartisan appropriations. Both approaches are documented in their own answers rather than assigned from their endorsement labels.

Lockwood foregrounds ending military interventions and particular arms support; Price foregrounds diplomacy, democratic institutions and displacement protections. These stated priorities do not prove opposite positions on an unmentioned specific intervention.
